title: Set APP_ENV at the top of tests/conftest.py, before any app import, not in a fixture
body:
## What happens

`app/db.py` builds its SQLAlchemy `engine` at import time from `get_settings()` in `app/config.py`, which reads `APP_ENV` once and is `@lru_cache`d. pytest imports `tests/conftest.py`, and through it `app.db`, during collection, before any fixture runs. When `APP_ENV` is set inside a fixture, the engine is already bound to the dev database, and tests fail with `psycopg.OperationalError: ... password authentication failed for user "ledger_dev"`.

CI does not show this because `.github/workflows/test.yml` sets `APP_ENV: test` for the whole job.

## Why the obvious fix does not work

Calling `get_settings.cache_clear()` in the fixture refreshes the settings object but not the module-level `engine` that was already built from the old one.

## What to do

Assign `os.environ["APP_ENV"] = "test"` on the first lines of `tests/conftest.py`, above every `app.*` import. Assign it rather than using `setdefault`, so a shell that exports `APP_ENV=dev` does not win.
